svg.title: CHISUM: Stern ramp: the hydraulic power pack as it stands, JS3-304 revision 1
svg.text: Stern ramp: the hydraulic power pack HPU-R as it stands, sheet 4 of 4 · JS3-304 · revision 1 · 12 November 2026
The hydraulic pump room on the main deck, port side, seen from above: every part numbered, every pipe named. Read with the operating instruction JS3-304-M1.
Forward to the right, the ship's side at the top. Metres from the transom.
the room's after half is kept for the cargo lift's power pack
HOW TO TELL THE LINES ABOARD
All oil lines are painted the same orange. Each is known by where it lies:
On the inboard wall, from the top of the bank down
cylinders, piston side: oil here lowers it
cylinders, rod side: oil here raises the ramp
Across the way at head height, to the tank
return, from the valve stand to the tank
pressure, from the pumps to the valve stand
Thin grey lines of 16 mm from each cylinder, cleat and latch are hoses: the last
half metre between a fixed line and a part that moves.

With V1 in its middle both of the ramp's lines are open to the tank: the ramp is then held by the load-holding valve bolted to each cylinder, not by the pumps. If the pressure reaches 210 bar the relief valve (8) lets the oil back into the tank.
THE PARTS, BY THEIR NUMBERS ON THE PLAN
What it does, and how it is known
About 1,500 litres of oil, on a drip tray (the broken line). Everything of the power pack stands on its lid or its sides. The level glass is on its inboard side, toward the way.
100 l/min at 210 bar, under a 37 kW motor that stands upright on the lid. One pump alone works the ramp at half speed.
As No. 1. With both running the ramp is raised from its lowest in about a minute and a half.
A small pump, 8 l/min at 160 bar, under a 4 kW motor: it works the ten cleats and lifts the two safety latches with the main pumps stopped.
One in each main pump's delivery, the dark body with a union nut each end: a pump that is stopped is not driven backwards by the one that runs.
The grey block on the lid's edge beside the way, where the pumps' deliveries meet. The pressure line P leaves its top; 7, 8 and 9 stand on it.
The dark bowl: 10 micron. Its clogging switch lights the alarm lamp on the starter panel (19) and gives the group alarm.
Under the red cap: it opens at 210 bar and lets oil back into the tank, so the pressure can never be more.
On a gauge cock (the red tee handle shuts it off) on the block's inboard edge: the pumps' pressure. 0 with the pumps stopped, about 195 bar with one running; red from 210.
On the tank's after end, with its 1.1 kW fan: the oil coming back is cooled by air before it goes into the tank.
25 micron, in the return into the tank, with a switch that says when it is clogged.
The yellow cap: where the tank breathes as its level goes up and down, and where it is filled.
On the tank's inboard side, with its lever: with no power the cleats are worked by it, and slowly the ramp.
On the inboard wall across the way. The seven lines leave its top: A, B, C, D and the conduit E go aft along the wall; P and T cross to the tank.

Lever to one side: oil to line A, the ramp is raised. To the other: oil to B, it is lowered. In the middle: both lines to the tank. Worked by its two solenoids from the control stand, or by the lever here.
Oil to line C locks the ten cleats; to line D lets them go and lifts the two safety latches.
For the ramp cover over the fixed ramp, which is not built. Its ports are plugged.
On the stand's top, each on its gauge cock: PG2 reads line A, which carries the leaf (189 bar with the ramp level); PG3 reads line B.
On the forward wall, at the end of the way: the isolator, a starter for each motor, the control transformer. Its two leaves open into the way.
On two posts over the power pack, 2.1 m up: the motors' cables from the starter panel, each coming down to its motor in a conduit.
Pressure block (6) to the valve stand (14)
The pumps' oil, at up to 210 bar, on its way to the valves.
The oil coming back from the valves. No pressure to speak of.
Valve stand to the rod side of both cylinders
Oil here pulls the cylinders in and RAISES the ramp. It also carries the leaf's weight while the ramp is down: gauge PG2 and the control stand's RAMP
Valve stand to the piston side of both cylinders
Oil here pushes the cylinders out and LOWERS the ramp, against the load-holding valves, which open only while B has pressure.
Valve stand to the ten cleats
Oil here shoots the eight bolts and closes the two hooks: the door is LOCKED.
Valve stand to the ten cleats and the two safety latches
Oil here draws the bolts, opens the hooks and lifts the latches: the door is FREE to be lowered.
Starter panel (19) to the control stand at the stern door
Not oil: the control stand's cables, carried with the pipes.
THE OIL, AND HOW MUCH OF IT
The yard's choice (stern_place.FLUID, TANK): not a maker's figures

ISO VG 46: mineral hydraulic oil of high viscosity index, type HVLP (DIN 51524 part 3; ISO 11158 class HV). Viscosity index 140 or more, pour point -33 °C or lower. Kept to ISO 4406 18/16/13 or cleaner, water under 0.1 %.
The tank holds about 1,460 litres to its lid (16.6 litres to the centimetre). With the cylinders and the lines full she takes about 1,650 litres in all.
0.76 m over the tank's bottom, 1,260 litres: where it is filled to with the ramp raised and locked, the rods in.
0.67 m, 1,120 litres: where it stands with the ramp level. Lowering the ramp takes the two rods' own volume out of the tank; it comes back when the ramp is raised.
0.60 m, 990 litres: the level switch. OIL LEVEL lights at the control stand, with the group alarm. Oil has been lost.
0.48 m, 790 litres: under this the pumps are not run; their suction strainers are 0.10 m over the bottom.
Works at 30 to 55 °C. The cooler's fan starts at 45 °C and stops at 40 °C. OIL TEMP alarm at 70 °C. Under 0 °C the oil is warmed by one pump before the ramp is worked.
Main relief valve 210 bar; the cleats' relief valve 160 bar; the load-holding valves 250 bar. A running pump holds about 195 bar; line A carries up to 198 bar.
WHERE THE MODEL IS SIMPLER THAN THE DIAGRAM (SHEET 2), SAID PLAINLY

· The return line T is drawn coming down beside P onto the pressure block. By the diagram it goes through the cooler (10) and the return filter (11) into the tank: that pipework on the lid is not drawn yet.
· The cleat pump (4) is drawn delivering into the same pressure block. By the diagram it has a line and a relief valve of its own (RV2, 160 bar) to the cleat valve V2: not drawn yet.

· The lines carry no markers aboard yet: they are told apart by where they lie (right). The valve stand's levers, the hand pump and the gauge cocks are drawn and are not worked on the page; the ramp is worked from its control stand.

· The level glass carries no marks yet and its level does not move with the ramp; the oil's temperature is not kept and the cooler's fan does not turn. Making the pack work in full is the next piece of work on it.
Made by ferry/yard/drawings/stern_drawing.py from ferry/blender/stern_place.py, ga.py and ferry/systems/stern.py (arrangement revision D): the numbers the model and the register are built from.
